verdict_text:
YES

The plan casts exactly the 112 projection matrices (7 per layer × 16 layers) to bfloat16 and leaves the other two tensors float32 (the leading `.*` → float32 cast is a no-op on an all-float32 input, and it runs before the bfloat16 cast), renames nothing, deletes nothing, and writes `out/T3` as sharded safetensors with a 256 MiB shard budget. The required checks are all enforced before writing: the count-112 assert plus the "all projections are bfloat16" and "everything else is float32" dtype asserts together imply exactly 112 bfloat16 tensors (given the count-114 assert), and the two named-tensor dtype asserts are present literally. The "exactly 112 bfloat16" check is expressed as that pair of dtype asserts rather than a direct count of bfloat16 tensors, but it is equivalent and still fails loudly on any deviation.
